title: Repeatability and retry-solver mechanism of the G21F admissibility islands

status6_mechanism.interpretation: Eight temporal-certificate rejections exhaust the configured retry ladder until the final physical attempt ends in a non-converged solver result; canonical result status 2 is then mapped to participant status 6.

bounded_conclusions: The six-island status-0/status-6 topology from G21F is deterministic for the frozen 33 binary64 heads: all three fresh immutable-origin sessions reproduce the status vector and island boundaries exactly.
The complete read-only backend observation snapshots are also repeatable across sessions in this frozen experiment.

Every status-6 head shares one aggregate mechanism: eight temporal rejections consume the retry ladder, followed by one final non-converged physical solver observation, with no mass rejection and no temporal-certificate-unavailable rejection.

Every status-0 head in the frozen scan shares one successful execution class: 20 accepted substeps, 100 attempts, 80 temporal rejections, zero solver rejections, and a converged final physical solver observation.

The local nonmonotone status topology is therefore not session nondeterminism. It is a deterministic bifurcation in the transaction/retry plus physical-solver execution path at binary64-adjacent head perturbations.
This result does not justify smoothing the islands, changing retry limits or temporal tolerances, selecting STANDARD versus NOUR, or production-admitting response-space globalization.
next_natural_unit: Preregister a representative adjacent-head physical-solver forensic diagnostic across one 6->0 and one 0->6 island boundary. Compare the final retry attempt at source-level solver diagnostics, Newton/backtracking trajectory and residual evolution to identify why solver status flips under sub-picometre head perturbations, without changing solver or transaction policy.
